briefings.title: 99.9% of the internet is about to be AI?
briefings.tldr: Alex Blania, CEO of Tools for Humanity and Co-Founder of Merge Labs, discusses the creation of a global "Proof of Human" network to combat an internet where 99.9% of traffic is AI-driven, while announcing a $250 million investment from OpenAI into Merge Labs to bridge biological and artificial intelligence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Alex Blania, CEO of Tools for Humanity and Co-Founder of Merge Labs, discusses the creation of a global "Proof of Human" network to combat an internet where 99.9% of traffic is AI-driven, while announcing a $250 million investment from OpenAI into Merge Labs to bridge biological and artificial intelligence.

## The World Ecosystem: Establishing a "Real Human Network"
* **The Core Problem:** Alex Blania asserts that because AI has passed the Turing test and can mimic human behavior perfectly, the internet requires a fundamental "Proof of Human" layer to maintain authenticity.
    * **Projected AI Dominance:** Blania predicts that nearly 99.9% of all internet traffic will eventually be AI-driven, making human-to-human interaction a premium feature.
    * **The Full Stack:** The ecosystem consists of **World ID** (the identity protocol), **World Chain** (the blockchain), and **World App** (the consumer-facing wallet and interface).
* **Privacy and Biometrics:** Blania addresses the controversy surrounding biometric data collection, calling privacy concerns the project's biggest misconception.
    * **Fundamental Anonymity:** The system is designed to be mathematically anonymous and privacy-preserving through advanced cryptography.
    * **Necessity of Biometrics:** Blania argues that biometrics are the only technical solution capable of solving the "Proof of Human" problem at a global scale.
* **Platform Integrations:** World ID is currently being integrated into major platforms.
    * **Tinder Japan:** A live integration allows users to prove they are real humans, verify profile pictures, and confirm their age.
    * **Future Verticals:** Key areas for integration include social networks, dating apps, gaming, and ticketing (e.g., Ticketmaster) to eliminate bot interference.

## Merge Labs: $250M Seed for Neural Research
* **Strategic Investment:** Merge Labs recently raised a $250 million seed round with direct investment from OpenAI (not its venture arm), signifying a deep research collaboration.
* **Mission and Technology:** The lab aims to bridge artificial and biological intelligence through high-bandwidth Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs).
    * **Technical Differentiation:** Unlike Neuralink’s mechanical threads, Merge Labs focuses on the combination of **ultrasound and molecular sensors** to interface with the brain.
    * **High-Bandwidth Goals:** The long-term objective is to move beyond the current "few thousand neurons" limit to interface with the entire brain, enabling significantly higher data transfer than a keyboard or screen.
* **Roadmap:** The company is currently structured as a research lab with a projected 15-year horizon.
    * **Phase 1:** Focused research on neural read/write capabilities.
    * **Phase 2:** Medical applications to assist those with disabilities or sensory loss.
    * **Phase 3:** Broad consumer applications as the successor to AR/VR technology.

## Operational Philosophy and Growth Metrics
* **Network Scaling:** World currently has 40 million users, with 17 million verified via "The Orb." Blania notes that the project's mission requires reaching hundreds of millions to billions to be truly successful.
* **Privacy as a "Fail-Safe":** One of the company's core operating principles is "fail-safe privacy." Blania believes a single data leak could "kill the company in a second," leading to a culture of extreme obsession with cryptographic security.
* **Leadership and Sam Altman:** Blania and Sam Altman have worked together for six years.
    * **Cadence:** They hold weekly in-depth strategy sessions covering every major decision, including hiring, fundraising, and partnerships.
    * **The "Hardcore" Approach:** Blania describes himself as "completely hardcore," forgoing social and personal life for the next five years to focus on the window of time leading up to the Singularity.

## The Future of Social Platforms
* **The Decay of X (Twitter):** Blania predicts that platforms like X will become "unusable" within months to two years unless they implement a technical proof-of-human solution.
* **Distinguishing vs. Combating:** The goal is not to eliminate bots—as Blania believes that is a "lost cause"—but to enable users to distinguish between authentic human content and AI agents.
* **Agentic Systems:** As AI systems become more agentic and open-source, the speed of platform degradation is expected to go "exponential."

> "I think platforms like X will not be usable in a matter of months, maximum two years, if they don't come up with completely new technical solutions." 
— **Alex Blania**

> "What’s so counterintuitive about what we’re doing here is that we have designed a system that can be fundamentally anonymous and is fundamentally anonymous and privacy preserving." 
— **Alex Blania**

> "We are probably in the last innings before superintelligence... this is an infinitely leveraged moment in time where any contribution you can make might actually make a meaningful impact." 
— **Alex Blania**

briefings.title: AI Can Change the Lives of the Poorest | Vinod Khosla  | Prannoy Roy
briefings.tldr: AI will act as the ultimate social equalizer in India, providing every citizen with free, high-quality healthcare and personalized education by 2030, provided the government adopts proactive policies to pivot from traditional IT outsourcing to AI service exports.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI will act as the ultimate social equalizer in India, providing every citizen with free, high-quality healthcare and personalized education by 2030, provided the government adopts proactive policies to pivot from traditional IT outsourcing to AI service exports.

## Universal Access to Expertise
* **The "Zero-Cost" Expertise Model:** Vinod Khosla predicts that by 2030, the cost of expertise in medicine, education, and law will trend toward zero. 
    * **Healthcare:** AI can provide free primary care and chronic disease management (diabetes, hypertension) through mobile devices, acting as a 24/7 personal doctor.
    * **Education:** AI tutors can offer highly personalized learning, identifying specific knowledge gaps and teaching in local dialects like Khasi or at specific educational levels (e.g., fifth-grade vs. university level).
* **AI as a Social Equalizer:** Khosla argues that while the rich currently have an advantage through private tutors and doctors, AI levels the playing field.
    * A farm worker and an oncologist will eventually use the same AI model, granting the poor access to the world’s best expertise.
    * AI often outperforms human doctors in diagnostics and can be more emotionally responsive or patient than time-constrained human professionals.

## Economic Transformation and the BPO Decline
* **The End of Traditional Outsourcing:** The current business models for Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) and IT services are expected to decline rapidly within five years as AI automates these functions.
* **The "AI Services Export" Opportunity:** India must pivot from exporting human labor to exporting AI services. 
    * **Sovereign AI:** Khosla highlights investments in companies like **Sarvam**, which is building AI models specifically for India’s regional languages and scripts.
    * **Speed of Growth:** He cites **Emergent**, an Indian software company that reached a $50 million run rate in just seven months, as a template for future growth.
* **Redefining GDP:** In a deflationary AI economy, traditional GDP may decline as services that once cost millions (like computing or expert advice) become nearly free, even as the actual production of goods and services increases.

## Physical World Constraints and Robotics
* **Software vs. Hardware Gap:** While "intelligence AI" (software) is ready today, "robotics AI" is approximately 5–7 years behind.
    * **Physical Interventions:** Complex surgeries and high-end physical diagnostics will still require human intervention (triage) or physical hospitals for the next decade.
    * **Infrastructure:** AI can eventually reduce costs in "hard" sectors like housing and transit by optimizing materials and enabling self-driving public transport (similar to a low-cost, AI-driven Uber/Ola service).

## Policy as the Primary Bottleneck
* **The "UPI" for Health and Education:** Khosla urges the Indian government to use the **Aadhaar/UPI** framework to deliver universal health and education services. 
* **Global Competition:** China has a centralized national goal for AI leadership; Khosla warns that if Indian voters or politicians reject AI due to fear of job losses, they will miss the massive welfare benefits.
* **Economic Mobility:** With the right policy, AI can drive unprecedented economic mobility by removing the cost barriers to elite education and professional advice.

## Notable Quotes

> "AI will be a big, big equalizer between the poorest and least educated and the most educated and most well-off... A farm worker will have access to the expertise of an oncologist because they are both using the same AI." — **Vinod Khosla**

> "The business of BPO or business process outsourcing will decline rapidly... India can take that [talent] to provide AI services to the rest of the world that's not as well equipped." — **Vinod Khosla**

> "When the AI tutor is cheap, maybe even free from a UPI-like service... then the poor person has a better tutor than the human tutor the rich people can hire." — **Vinod Khosla**

> "I think the cost of primary care can be down to—it shouldn't cost more than tens of rupees per month to provide this service... This is not hundreds of rupees per month. It'll be that cheap by 2030." — **Vinod Khosla**

briefings.title: Anthropic Builder Summit Bengaluru | CEO Dario Amodei & Rahul Patil Keynote
briefings.tldr: India has emerged as Anthropic’s second-largest global user base, characterized by high technical intensity and a rapid shift from basic AI assistance to complex, agentic "thinking" software that solves large-scale societal and industrial problems.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
India has emerged as Anthropic’s second-largest global user base, characterized by high technical intensity and a rapid shift from basic AI assistance to complex, agentic "thinking" software that solves large-scale societal and industrial problems.

## India as a Global AI Powerhouse
*   **Rapid Growth and Adoption:** Anthropic’s run-rate revenue in India has doubled in the last four months, with 50% of user conversations focused on computational and mathematical work.
    *   **GitHub Impact:** Approximately 4% of all global GitHub commits are now wired through Claude, a figure that doubled in just one month.
    *   **Language Support:** Anthropic has integrated 10 Indic languages (including Hindi, Bengali, Malayalam, and Gujarati) to cater to the region's multilingual diversity.
*   **Unique Market Intensity:** CEO Dario Amodei noted that Indian developers exhibit a higher degree of "technical intensity" compared to global averages, focusing heavily on API usage and production-grade software.
*   **Government Agility:** The Ministry of Statistics is currently building a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to query economic data, demonstrating faster governmental tech adoption than many Western counterparts.

## The Shift to Agentic AI and "Thinking" Software
*   **Beyond Chatbots:** The industry is moving from software that simply executes code to software that interprets, decides, and reasons.
*   **Three Pillars of Agent Infrastructure:** CTO Rahul Patil outlined the core components of the next generation of AI agents:
    *   **Contextual Intelligence:** Developing organizational and episodic memory so that "Day 100" of using an agent is significantly more effective than "Day 1."
    *   **Long-Running Execution:** Enabling agents to perform multi-week tasks, such as running A/B tests or scientific experiments, with autonomous iteration.
    *   **Genuine Collaboration:** Moving toward "transparent reasoning" where agents push back against users when they are wrong, serving as true thinking partners.
*   **Ambient AI:** Future iterations of Claude will likely move beyond keyboard interfaces and chat boxes to "Ambient Claude," which operates subtly behind the scenes to facilitate workflows.

## Anthropic’s "Real Work" Philosophy
*   **Productive vs. Addictive AI:** Anthropic distinguishes its models by focusing on "productive work" (coding, legal, medicine) rather than "short-term addictive entertainment."
    *   **Model Tiers:**
        *   **Opus:** The smartest model for advanced research and complex problem-solving.
        *   **Sonnet:** The "default" production model balancing speed and intelligence.
        *   **Haiku:** Designed for massive, planet-scale distribution and speed.
*   **Safety as a Prerequisite:** Both speakers emphasized that safety is not an afterthought but a core design principle. Anthropic frequently delays model releases until they are 100% certain of their safety guardrails.
*   **Skating Where the Puck is Going:** Amodei advised enterprises not to build for current AI capabilities but to design for the capabilities expected in two years, automating entire end-to-end workflows rather than small sub-tasks.

## Sector Impact and Social Benefit
*   **Life Sciences and Health:** AI is expected to compress 100 years of medical innovation into just 5-10 years. In India, startups like Saket are already using Claude to identify clinical markers that prevent hospitalizations.
*   **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI):** Building on the success of Aadhaar and UPI, India is applying AI to public services.
    *   **Adalat AI:** An initiative making legal information across thousands of court cases and multiple languages accessible to common citizens.
    *   **Udyam Learning Foundation:** Using AI to teach business thinking to youth in the 16-25 age bracket.
    *   **Ekstep Foundation:** Applying AI to agriculture to help small farmers increase productivity through specialized digital infrastructure.

> "Software is not just executing to the code that is being written. Software is actually thinking, it's interpreting, and it's deciding. And when software begins to think, trust is no longer something that you can take for granted." — **Rahul Patil**

> "Don’t build for step four out of a 10-step workflow, try and do the whole workflow even if the AI model isn't quite capable of it yet... Skate where the puck is going." — **Dario Amodei**

> "Everything that has been invented so far is going to feel so insignificant compared to everything else that's going to happen [in the next 5-10 years]." — **Rahul Patil**

briefings.title: Conférence d'Arthur Mensch, cofondateur et pdg de Mistral AI, à l'École polytechnique.
briefings.tldr: Arthur Mensch argues that AI is rapidly commoditizing traditional intellectual and engineering tasks, necessitating a shift toward higher levels of abstraction and human-centric problem-solving to maintain European strategic and cultural sovereignty.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Arthur Mensch argues that AI is rapidly commoditizing traditional intellectual and engineering tasks, necessitating a shift toward higher levels of abstraction and human-centric problem-solving to maintain European strategic and cultural sovereignty.

## The Evolution of AI: From Chatbots to Operating Systems
* **Commoditization of Intellect:** The current generation of engineers has effectively commoditized their own original skill sets—calculation, synthesis, and basic software development.
    * AI systems are currently gaining approximately one "year of seniority" every year in terms of the complexity of tasks they can automate.
    * The time-horizon of automatable intellectual tasks is doubling roughly every six months.
* **Paradigm Shift in Software:** We are moving away from writing code to define applications and toward a world where AI identifies the problem, processes the data, and generates the interface itself.
* **AI as an OS:** Mensch views generative AI not merely as a chatbot, but as a "system of discovery" or a new operating system capable of navigating the web, interacting with humans via empathy, and autonomously managing information systems.
* **Educational Requirements:** Students must learn to work both with and without AI. Manual, "computer-free" reasoning remains essential for developing the cognitive capacity to manage the machines.

## Strategic Career Paths in the AI Era
* **Developing AI (The Interdisciplinary Frontier):** The most significant opportunities lie at the intersection of AI and "hard" sciences like material physics, biotechnology, and quantum mechanics.
    * Most current AI progress is "biased" because it was built by computer scientists to solve computer science problems; the next frontier is vertical specialization in physical world simulators.
* **Integrating AI (Organizational Transformation):** There is a massive shortage of talent capable of re-engineering industrial and public service processes (healthcare, finance, defense) to leverage AI for productivity gains.
* **Human-Centric Alternatives:** Mensch rejects "techno-solutionism." He highlights critical sectors where AI plays a minor role, such as elder care, climate change mitigation, and high-touch human services.
* **The Value of the PhD:** Mensch strongly recommends doctoral studies as a foundation for entrepreneurship, noting that a thesis teaches one how to "struggle," design a long-term project, and see it through to completion.

## Sovereignty, Defense, and Cultural Influence
* **Industrial Independence:** To remain competitive, Europe must have its own AI infrastructure. Relying on foreign entities with "disputable strategic alignment" creates a dangerous economic dependency.
* **Dual-Use and Defense:** AI is a strategic deterrent. Mensch notes that as adversaries deploy autonomous systems on the battlefield, Europe must develop similar capabilities to maintain the balance of power, despite the moral complexities of "lethality" in AI.
* **The Battle for Influence:** AI systems are the new gateways to information, replacing traditional search engines. 
    * **Cultural Control:** If only two global entities control the portals through which the next generation accesses information, they possess excessive "thought control" incompatible with democracy.
    * **Resisting the Decline Narrative:** Mensch criticizes the "narrative of decline" often pushed from across the Atlantic, urging European innovators to stay and build in Europe rather than contributing to the "technological colonization" by the U.S.

## The "Non-Glorious" Realities of Entrepreneurship
* **From Coder to Organizer:** Entrepreneurship quickly transitions from technical work to organizational management. Technical founders must accept that their primary role will eventually become sales, external relations, and recruiting.
* **Problem-First Methodology:** Mistral AI initially started with a solution searching for a problem; Mensch advises that it is far more effective to start with a human or industrial problem and work back to the technical solution.
* **Sales and Resilience:** Selling is the most leveraged task in a startup because it generates the revenue required for growth.
    * Founders must develop "psychological resilience" to handle the asymmetry of being a creator in a world of critics; entrepreneurship is described as "90% struggle and 10% success."
* **Hyper-growth Management:** Growing from 0 to 600 people in three years creates "organizational heat," requiring leaders to constantly delegate the technical tasks they originally loved to avoid becoming a bottleneck.

> "Since 2023, we can consider that the systems we put in place gain one year of seniority every year. This means many tasks are being replaced or must evolve significantly, starting with the engineering and intellectual professions." — Arthur Mensch

> "Technology in the United States is conceived as a vector of power and a vector of colonization. Conceiving one's action and career to reverse these power dynamics is one of the things that guided my action." — Arthur Mensch

> "The job of an entrepreneur is generally 90% struggle and 10% success. This aspect of 'not succeeding' is something one learns very well during a PhD." — Arthur Mensch

briefings.title: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46
briefings.tldr: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are "statistical parrots" that lack human-style reasoning, their ability to navigate unstructured data and act as "agentic" tools provides immense corporate value today, regardless of whether the technology ever achieves human-level superintelligence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** While Large Language Models (LLMs) are "statistical parrots" that lack human-style reasoning, their ability to navigate unstructured data and act as "agentic" tools provides immense corporate value today, regardless of whether the technology ever achieves human-level superintelligence.

## The Technical Reality: How LLMs "Think"
*   **The Autocomplete Engine:** LLMs are essentially sophisticated autocomplete tools. They don't "know" facts; they predict the next most likely word (token) based on patterns found in massive datasets.
    *   **High Energy Costs:** To generate the 10,000th word in a conversation, the model must re-process all 9,999 previous words, which is why AI remains computationally expensive.
*   **The Role of Embeddings:** Words are converted into "embeddings"—numerical scores on an "XY axis" (graph paper) that represent a word's "vibe" or meaning. 
    *   **Contextual Understanding:** The "Transformer" architecture (pioneered by Google in 2017) allows models to weigh these embeddings against each other to understand context (e.g., the difference between "a fruit date" and "a calendar date").
*   **The Hallucination Paradox:** Hallucinations are not bugs; they are a feature of how these models work. Because they prioritize "vibe" and statistical probability over logic, the surprise is not that they hallucinate, but that they ever provide correct answers at all.
    *   **Logic Gaps:** Guetta cites a "ball in a bag" probability test where LLMs fail basic math despite sounding confident, proving they lack a true internal "world model."

## The Scaling Debate: Guetta vs. Gary Marcus
*   **Diminishing Returns:** Guetta largely agrees with critic Gary Marcus that current LLM architecture (predicting the next word) may face diminishing returns and might never scale to "Superintelligence" or human-level reasoning.
*   **Benchmarking Limitations:** Current "intelligence" is measured by benchmarks like the MMLU (essentially an SAT exam). Guetta argues that doing well on a test is not the same as having the creativity or situational awareness of a human professional.
*   **Value vs. Intelligence:** Guetta’s central thesis is that "Superintelligence" is a distraction. Even if models never get "smarter" than they are today, they are already "good enough" to transform the global economy.

## Three Buckets of Business Value
*   **Supercharging Classical Machine Learning:** Using GenAI to extract meaning from unstructured text (like reviews or PDFs) and feeding that data into old-school predictive models.
    *   **Example:** Content moderation. Instead of just looking for "bad words," GenAI can understand the intent behind a message, making automated moderation far more accurate.
*   **Agentic AI ("AI with Hands"):** This is the next frontier. It involves giving an LLM access to IT "pipes" so it can execute tasks in the real world.
    *   **Capability:** A travel agent bot that doesn't just suggest a flight but actually calls an API to book the ticket, process the credit card, and send the confirmation email.
*   **Specialized Chatbots and RAG:** Using "Retrieval-Augmented Generation" to allow a model to "read" thousands of internal company documents and answer specific questions about contracts, risk, or operations.

## Market Impacts and Corporate Hurdles
*   **Software and Moats:** Software giants like Salesforce face a "speed of light" problem. While the cost of developing code is collapsing due to AI, their true value may shift toward providing the "human structure" and verified databases that AI cannot replicate.
*   **The "Dirty Data" Problem:** The biggest bottleneck to AI adoption is not the technology, but corporate IT. Most companies have "messy" data spread across multiple legacy systems.
    *   **The Silver Lining:** Guetta notes that AI is actually being used to clean this data (e.g., identifying that "Coke," "Coca-Cola," and "CCNA" are the same entity), finally allowing companies to organize their internal knowledge.
*   **Management Consulting:** While AI can replace basic information retrieval, Guetta believes consultants still provide value by "getting the right people in a room" to make decisions—a human function AI cannot fulfill.

## Notable Quotes

> "What you should be surprised by is that [LLMs] ever *don't* hallucinate... The fact they ever get it right is crazy." — **Daniel Guetta**

> "I’m not as worried about artificial intelligence as I am about human stupidity—giving those models a tool [without safeguards]." — **Daniel Guetta**

> "If you told me today these models will never get better, they will hallucinate forever... there is still so much value that you can capture." — **Daniel Guetta**

> "We are building a car—or learning how to drive a car—while it's being built. Every five seconds you sneeze and there's a new kind of AI that totally changes your offering." — **Daniel Guetta**

briefings.title: How to Position for Major Market Rotations | Macro Mondays, Feb. 16, 2026
briefings.tldr: Markets are entering a "Goldilocks" regime characterized by accelerating US cyclical growth and cooling inflation, driving a rotation out of high-CapEx "hyperscalers" and into the AI supply chain, energy, and global bonds.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Markets are entering a "Goldilocks" regime characterized by accelerating US cyclical growth and cooling inflation, driving a rotation out of high-CapEx "hyperscalers" and into the AI supply chain, energy, and global bonds.

## The AI "Kiss of Death" and Market Rotations
* **Sector Disruption:** AI is causing rapid valuation shifts as it moves from sector to sector, recently hitting SaaS, financial services, and logistics.
    * A recent white paper from a trucking firm suggested AI could increase shipping volumes by 300% without adding costs, causing a massive sell-off in traditional trucking stocks.
* **The Mag 7 CapEx Problem:** The "hyperscalers" are seeing free cash flow in "freefall" due to massive infrastructure and R&D spending on proprietary chips.
    * **Market Sentiment:** A survey of investors shows a 50/50 split on whether the greater risk is over-investing or under-investing in AI. 
    * **Investment Strategy:** Andreas Steno suggests buying the "supply chain" of the Mag 7 (those receiving the CapEx) rather than the companies spending the cash, until the returns on that investment become visible.
* **Automation Progress:** Steno notes that 90–95% of typical macroeconomic research tasks have been automated by AI agents within the last 18 months.

## Macro Outlook: Inflation and Rates
* **Softening Inflation:** Despite concerns over tariffs, seven of the last ten inflation reports have come in softer than expected.
    * **Data Outliers:** A recent spike in transportation services (1.35%) was driven by record increases in auto registration and parking fees, which are viewed as statistical outliers rather than a trend.
    * **Nowcast:** Current data models suggest a 90% probability that inflation will continue to fall relative to the most recent print.
* **Monetary Policy Timing:** The market does not expect significant rate cuts until Kevin Warsh takes power in June 2026.
    * **Powell’s Legacy:** There is a feasible scenario where Jerome Powell attempts to "orchestrate" one final rate cut before leaving office to cement a soft landing.

## Geopolitical Realignment and the "New World Order"
* **US-Europe Decoupling:** Comments by Marco Rubio in Munich—stating "friends pay for their own beers"—signal a shift where Europe must fund its own defense. 
    * This represents a loss of US leverage; if the US stops "buying the beers," it loses the right to decide the strategic direction of the alliance.
* **The Russia-China Pivot:** There is a growing strategic push (aligned with Donald Trump’s views) to reintegrate Russia into the global trade and SWIFT system.
    * **Geopolitical Logic:** Similar to Nixon’s 1970s China pivot, the goal is to pull Russia away from China’s sphere of influence, even if it requires "holding one's nose" regarding the Ukraine conflict.
* **Middle East Tensions:** The deployment of two US carrier task forces near Iran suggests the US is building the capability for a prolonged conflict, not just a "hit and run" attack.

## Asset Class Strategy
* **Oil as Top Trade:** Crude oil is currently flagged as the best risk-reward trade due to the US domestic recovery and its utility as a "tail hedge" against Iranian conflict.
* **The Bear Case for Gold:** A peace deal in Ukraine is cited as the single biggest risk to the gold trade.
    * If Russia is reintegrated into the dollar system and its reserves are no longer under threat of confiscation, the urgency for central bank gold hoarding diminishes.
* **Global Bonds:** For the first time in a long period, macro nowcasts have flipped positive on global bonds, benefiting from AI’s potential deflationary impact on the CPI.
* **Cyclical Equities:** Strength is appearing in the Polish (EPOL) and Korean (EWY) ETFs, signaling a broadening manufacturing recovery alongside the semiconductor boom.

> "The market does not buy into [CapEx] until they see the results on the other side... Mag 7s will be tricky to buy as long as they spend this much, but they will probably turn into huge investment cases once they start harvesting the returns." — Andreas Steno

> "If you don't buy the beers, you don't get to decide where we all go. So that is the shift that we're seeing [in US-Europe relations]." — Mikkel Rosenvold

> "The biggest risk to the gold trade is a peace in Ukraine. Because the war in Ukraine was what started this gold trade." — Andreas Steno

briefings.title: LIVE: Viktor Orbán and Marco Rubio deliver joint remarks in Budapest
briefings.tldr: Hungary and the United States have entered a diplomatic "Golden Age" following the signing of a bilateral civil nuclear pact and a shared commitment to peace in Ukraine, driven by the close personal relationship between Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and the U.S. administration.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Hungary and the United States have entered a diplomatic "Golden Age" following the signing of a bilateral civil nuclear pact and a shared commitment to peace in Ukraine, driven by the close personal relationship between Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and the U.S. administration.

## A "Golden Age" of Bilateral Relations
*   **Highest Level of Cooperation:** Prime Minister Viktor Orbán described current U.S.–Hungary relations as the most balanced and friendly in over 30 years, attributing this shift to the personal rapport between himself and the U.S. President.
*   **Personal Leadership:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that the "person-to-person connection" between the two leaders has been the primary catalyst for the current "Golden Era," moving beyond rhetoric into tangible action.
*   **Diplomatic Reciprocity:** 
    *   Hungarians can once again travel to the U.S. without a visa.
    *   Orbán has been invited to the inaugural "Board of Peace" meeting in Washington D.C.
    *   An open invitation remains for the U.S. President to visit Budapest.

## Strategic Energy and Economic Cooperation
*   **Civilian Nuclear Pact:** The primary purpose of the visit was the formal signing of a cooperation agreement to facilitate Hungary's civilian nuclear program, signed by Secretary Rubio and Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó.
*   **Energy Security:**
    *   **Russian Exemptions:** Orbán highlighted that U.S.-provided exceptions allow Hungary to continue using Russian gas and oil, ensuring cheap energy for domestic industry and households.
    *   **Regional Infrastructure:** The leaders discussed the potential acquisition of the Serbian refinery (NIS) by the Hungarian oil company MOL.
*   **Investment Milestones:** Rubio noted that 17 major U.S. investments have been decided upon in Hungary over the past year—a decade-long record—refuting claims that Hungary is internationally isolated.

## Peace Efforts and the Ukraine Conflict
*   **Diplomatic Resolution:** Both leaders emphasized that the U.S. is uniquely positioned to bring both sides of the Russian-Ukrainian war to the table.
    *   Orbán offered Budapest as a potential venue for a future peace summit.
    *   Rubio confirmed that technical-level military talks between the warring parties have already occurred in the Middle East with U.S. facilitation.
*   **The "Trump Factor":** Both speakers asserted their belief that the war would never have broken out had Donald Trump been in office at the time, and that his leadership is currently the only viable path to a peaceful conclusion.
*   **Board of Peace:** Hungary is an "indispensable" founding member of the Board of Peace, a role Rubio credited to Orbán's willingness to engage geopolitically when other nations hesitate.

## Addressing Strategic Rivals and Domestic Sovereignty
*   **China and Diversification:** 
    *   **Orbán’s Stance:** Hungary maintains a policy of "open cards," cooperating with China on trade while strictly limiting security cooperation to NATO allies.
    *   **Rubio’s Response:** While the U.S. seeks to diversify supply chains to avoid over-dependence on any one nation, Rubio stated the U.S. does not expect allies to completely isolate themselves from China, provided national interests remain the priority.
*   **Iran Nuclear Negotiations:** Rubio expressed skepticism regarding a potential deal with Iran, citing the difficulty of negotiating with "radical Shia clerics" who prioritize theology over geopolitics, though he confirmed the U.S. continues to pursue a diplomatic path.
*   **National Interest as a Standard:** Rubio defended the "America First" and "Hungary First" approaches, stating that a leader who does not act in their own nation's interest "won't be leader for long."

> "A new golden age has set upon us concerning the relationship between the United States and Hungary... I cannot remember, although for 30 odd years I have been present in politics, when the last time it was that the relationships between the two nations were at such a high level." — **Viktor Orbán**

> "The relationship between the United States and Hungary today is as close as I can possibly imagine it being. And it's not just close rhetorically, it's close in action... President Trump is deeply committed to your success because your success is our success." — **Marco Rubio**

> "Usually when you're trying to end wars the international community applauds you. This is one of the few wars I've ever seen where some people in the international community condemn you for trying to help end a war." — **Marco Rubio**

> "The Ukrainians quite rightly believe that what government Hungary shall have is significant to them... we must acknowledge that the Ukrainian President and Ukraine will be an active participant of this election and we have to prevail against them too." — **Viktor Orbán**

briefings.title: Lyn Alden: How to Survive The Gradual Print Era — Fed Chair Warsh, Gold & Bitcoin
briefings.tldr: The global economy is entering a "gradual print" era within a sovereign debt crisis, characterized by eroding Federal Reserve independence and a shift toward a multipolar monetary order where gold and Bitcoin serve as neutral reserve assets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global economy is entering a "gradual print" era within a sovereign debt crisis, characterized by eroding Federal Reserve independence and a shift toward a multipolar monetary order where gold and Bitcoin serve as neutral reserve assets.

## The Macro Context: A "Fourth Turning" Debt Cycle
*   **The 80-Year Cycle:** Lyn Alden argues the world is currently in a "Fourth Turning"—a chaotic, intergenerational phase change that aligns with Ray Dalio’s long-term debt cycle.
    *   **Sovereign Debt Crisis:** This period is defined by high debt-to-GDP ratios and the exhaustion of traditional monetary tools (interest rates at zero).
    *   **Institutional Distrust:** Public trust in media, Congress, and corporations is at historic lows, mirroring the social upheavals of the 1930s and 1940s.
*   **Shift to Public Debt:** We have moved from the "private debt" bubble (2008) to a "sovereign debt" bubble. Because governments rarely default nominally, the primary outcome is currency devaluation and purchasing power debasement.
*   **Demographic & Tech Pressures:** Unlike previous cycles, this turning includes shrinking global demographics and the "real-time chaos" of social media, which accelerates the memetic downfall of institutional norms.

## Fed Independence and the 1940s Parallel
*   **The Powell-Trump Clash:** Alden identifies Jerome Powell’s recent public resistance to executive pressure as the most direct clash between the Fed and the White House since the 1951 Treasury-Fed Accord.
    *   **Soft Capture:** While the Fed is more independent than it was during WWII (when it was a literal arm of the Treasury), high fiscal dominance is leading to a "soft capture" where political influence dictates rate policy.
*   **Kevin Warsh as Nominee:** Alden analyzes the potential impact of Trump’s Fed Chair nominee, Kevin Warsh.
    *   **Policy Divergence:** She expects Warsh to be **dovish on interest rates** (using AI-driven productivity gains as a justification for cuts) but potentially **hawkish on the balance sheet** (attempting to limit QE).
    *   **Populist Rhetoric:** Warsh’s criticism of the Fed’s "Wall Street-centric" policies aligns with the populist movement to refocus monetary policy on "Main Street."
*   **The "Gradual Print":** Alden’s base case is not a massive "money printer" event, but a steady, gradual increase in the Fed’s balance sheet as they reach the floor of quantitative tightening.

## The Multipolar Monetary Order: Gold vs. Bitcoin
*   **The End of the Triffin Dilemma:** The US dollar is increasingly unable to serve as the sole global reserve currency. This is forcing a shift toward a multipolar system where neutral assets bridge different currency blocs (US, China, Europe).
*   **Gold’s Resurgence:**
    *   **Central Bank Accumulation:** Sovereigns like China are holding fewer Treasuries and more gold to gain "sovereign wiggle room" following the freezing of Russian reserves.
    *   **Market Sentiment:** Alden views the recent gold price surge as a "revaluation from undervalued to fairly valued," though she warns of a "local bubble" driven by momentum and the yen carry trade.
*   **Bitcoin’s Performance:**
    *   **Cycle Disappointment:** Alden admits Bitcoin underperformed her $150,000 target this cycle, peaking at $126,000. She attributes this to the "four-year cycle" becoming a self-fulfilling psychological hurdle rather than a fundamental one.
    *   **Quantum Risk:** While technically manageable, Alden notes that institutional buyers are increasingly pricing in "left-tail" risks regarding quantum computing, which has suppressed some large-scale positions.

## Investment Strategy for a Chaotic Era
*   **Hard Assets and Energy:** Alden remains long on gold, silver, platinum, and Bitcoin, but she is currently leaning into "boring" real-world infrastructure like natural gas pipelines.
*   **The AI Capital Trap:** She warns that the "capital-light" era of Big Tech (Google, Meta) is ending.
    *   **CapEx War:** Companies are now forced into massive capital expenditures to compete in AI, meaning the "winners" of the tech war may see thinner margins than they did during the social media boom.
*   **Selective Equity Exposure:**
    *   **Emerging Markets:** She highlights Latin American banks as a surprise winner in the current trade war environment.
    *   **Cash Equivalents:** Alden maintains a "dry powder" position in cash equivalents but has moved from being a "super bear" to a "lukewarm bear" on long-duration bonds after five years of market devastation.

## Notable Quotes
> "We are basically in the fourth turning... sovereign debt crises tend to lead to more war, and war also can lead to sovereign debt crises. These things feed off each other." — **Lyn Alden**

> "Central bank rates are literally price controls on the price and time of money... they’re the most important price controls around." — **Lyn Alden**

> "I’ve been terming this the 'gradual print.' We have shifted away from Fed balance sheet reduction toward gradual Fed balance sheet increases." — **Lyn Alden**

> "You can meme about the downfall of empires in real time. That’s why it feels like everything is happening all at once." — **Lyn Alden**

briefings.title: PM Modi’s Mega Address At AI Summit 2026 LIVE: Focus On Innovation, Ethics & India’s Tech Future
briefings.tldr: India is positioning itself as the leader of a "Sovereign AI" movement, prioritizing the democratization of technology and affordable, multilingual, and offline-capable solutions designed specifically to address the challenges of the Global South while challenging the monopolies of Western and Chinese AI models.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
India is positioning itself as the leader of a "Sovereign AI" movement, prioritizing the democratization of technology and affordable, multilingual, and offline-capable solutions designed specifically to address the challenges of the Global South while challenging the monopolies of Western and Chinese AI models.

## The "India Model" of AI: Democratization vs. Monopoly
*   **Sovereign Strategy:** Unlike the high-cost, for-profit Western model or the opaque Chinese model, India is building a "Sovereign AI" system focused on *Sarvajan Sukhay, Sarvajan Hitay* (the welfare of all).
*   **Democratization of Tech:** The government aims to replicate the success of the Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI/UPI) by creating a "Common Compute" platform, allowing students, startups, and researchers access to tools without being beholden to Big Tech.
*   **Market Positioning:** India seeks to be a "Trust Partner," offering safe and transparent AI models that address the security and privacy concerns often associated with other global players.
*   **Accountability:** Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw emphasized that global platforms (like Netflix/OTTs) and AI developers must adhere to local laws and cultural contexts of the countries where they operate, rather than just the laws of their country of incorporation.

## Indigenous Innovation: Sarvam AI & Bharat Gen
*   **Multilingual Capabilities:** The **Sarvam AI** "Bulbul" model supports 11 Indian languages with over 93% accuracy, outperforming many Western chatbots that lack local linguistic depth.
*   **Offline Accessibility:** A significant breakthrough highlighted is Sarvam’s ability to run offline on smartphones and laptops, ensuring AI utility in remote areas without stable internet or cloud dependencies.
*   **Bharat Gen & Param 2:** These initiatives focus on building India’s indigenous hardware and software stack. By leveraging the **Param 2 supercomputer**, India is developing scalable models that avoid the expensive subscription traps of Western AI tools.
*   **Wadhwani AI:** This tool is already impacting five states, focusing on social sectors:
    *   **Healthcare:** Measuring infant malnutrition and managing TB.
    *   **Agriculture:** Pest management for cotton farmers and weather forecasting.

## Infrastructure and Economic Strategy
*   **Cost Efficiency:** India’s data center costs are reportedly half the global average. The country is targeting a 30-40% reduction in global costs for GPU and hardware manufacturing.
*   **Hardware Ambitions:** Through the **India Semi-Conductor Mission**, the government is pushing for self-sufficiency in chip production to ensure the AI journey includes hardware sovereignty, not just software development.
*   **Startup Ecosystem:** From the 2016 "Startup India" launch to the 1.5 lakh startups today, the focus is shifting to "Impact AI" where startups prioritize social outcomes over just technical capacity.
*   **Venture Capital Shift:** There has been a massive increase in local VC presence (from ~15 to over 1,000 VCs), supporting the "Seed Capital" and "Series A" needs of indigenous AI founders.

## Sector-Specific AI Integration
*   **Education (NEP 2020):** AI is being introduced from Class 3, with skill-building starting in Class 6. The government is expanding **Atal Tinkering Labs** from 10,000 to 20,000, with substantial funding for smart classrooms and hands-on "tinkering" kits.
*   **Agriculture:** The **Bharat Vistar** fund will launch AI chatbots like "Bhashini" or "Bharati" to help farmers solve local problems in their native dialects.
*   **Governance:** AI will be used to eliminate duplication in welfare schemes and streamline the Public Distribution System (PDS), with pilot projects already running in Gujarat for AI-managed ration tokens.

## Notable Quotes

> "India does not follow the Western model of for-profit monopoly. We believe in the democratization of technology... so that the benefit reaches the last person in a tribal village through their own local language." — **Pranav Bhatia, Startup Founder**

> "Content creators and OTT platforms must follow the local laws and cultural context of the country they are operating in... you cannot just rely on the laws of where you are incorporated." — **Ashwini Vaishnaw, Minister of Electronics & IT**

> "We don’t need the massive, ultra-costly AI models found in the West. India needs scalable, affordable models that solve 'Grand Challenges' locally for our people and the Global South." — **Ajay, CNN-News18 Correspondent**

> "Earlier, people spoke about roadmaps; now, everyone is talking about 'Impact.' Most products here are coming from startups focused on the social fabric rather than just data sets." — **Lt. Gen. (Retd) SP Kochhar**

briefings.title: Reporter Asks Marco Rubio: Is There U.S. Agreement That Greenland Will Not Be Ceded By Denmark?
briefings.tldr: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reported a "historic" joint meeting between Syrian authorities and Kurdish leaders to secure thousands of ISIS prisoners, while Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico accused Ukraine of using energy transit as "political blackmail" against Central European nations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary of State Marco Rubio reported a "historic" joint meeting between Syrian authorities and Kurdish leaders to secure thousands of ISIS prisoners, while Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico accused Ukraine of using energy transit as "political blackmail" against Central European nations.

## U.S. Diplomatic Strategy in Syria
*   **High-Level Mediation:** Secretary Rubio highlighted a historic meeting in Munich where the Syrian Foreign Minister (Al-Shara) and Kurdish leader General Mazloum met together with U.S. officials.
*   **Pragmatic Engagement:** Rubio defended the decision to work with interim Syrian authorities over the alternative of state collapse.
    *   **Avoiding Chaos:** The U.S. goal is to prevent Syria from becoming a "playground for terrorists" or seeing the return of Iranian influence.
*   **Security Successes:** Engagement with Al-Shara led to a cessation of fighting that allowed for the transfer of 4,000–5,000 ISIS prisoners to Iraq, preventing a massive jailbreak.
*   **Implementation Challenges:** The U.S. is pushing for a reintegration agreement between the Kurds and the national Syrian forces, alongside similar deals for the Druze, Bedouin, and Alawite populations.

## Greenland and Denmark Sovereignty
*   **Optimistic Trajectory:** Secretary Rubio confirmed ongoing high-level meetings with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark in Munich.
*   **Confidential Negotiations:** Rubio declined to provide specifics regarding the potential "ceding" of Greenlandic sovereignty to the U.S., stating he would not conduct sensitive diplomacy through the media.

## Energy Security and the Druzhba Pipeline
*   **Economic Impact:** Prime Minister Fico reported that the cessation of Russian gas transit through Ukraine has cost Slovakia €500 million annually in transit fees.
*   **Political Blackmail:** Fico alleged that the disruption of oil and gas flows through Ukraine is being used as a lever to pressure Hungary and Slovakia.
    *   **Hungarian Pressure:** Fico suggested that the restoration of energy flows may be tied to Hungary’s consent regarding Ukraine’s EU membership.
*   **Infrastructure Status:** Despite reports that Ukraine has repaired damaged sections of the pipeline, Fico expressed skepticism over the "political will" to resume flows.
*   **Humanitarian Aid:** Despite the financial losses, Fico noted that Slovakia continues to provide Ukraine with emergency electricity and gas to support civilians during the winter.

## EU Enlargement and Regional Tensions
*   **Ukraine’s EU Candidacy:** Slovakia maintains that Ukraine must meet all standard accession conditions without special shortcuts.
*   **Comparative Readiness:** PM Fico asserted that Balkan nations like Serbia, Montenegro, and Albania are "100 times better prepared" for EU membership than Ukraine.
*   **Infrastructure Control:** Fico suggested that post-war decisions must address the ownership of pipelines to ensure they cannot be used as "blackmail instruments" against sovereign states.

## Notable Quotes
> "We had two choices in Syria. Choice number one was to let the place fall apart... Choice number two is to try to see if it was possible to work with these interim authorities... Guess what? We chose number two because it's what made sense." — **Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State**

> "We've been able to move those prisoners into Iraq and out of harm's way so that we don't have a massive jailbreak and four or five thousand ISIS killers running crazy all over the place." — **Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State**

> "I perceive [current oil disruptions] as a political blackmailing towards Hungary because of the non-compromising approach of Hungary and membership of Ukraine to the EU." — **Robert Fico, Prime Minister of Slovakia**

> "We cannot lie now to Serbia, we cannot lie to Montenegro, we cannot lie to Albania—those countries are 100 times better prepared for accession than Ukraine." — **Robert Fico, Prime Minister of Slovakia**
